briefs.title: US real GDP revised up to 4.3% annual rate in Q3 2026 from 3.4%, BEA second estimate
briefs.summary: BEA's second estimate shows real GDP increased at an annual rate of 4.3% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 2.2% in the second quarter. The figure was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the 3.4% advance estimate, mainly reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 5.8%, while the PCE price index rose 2.1% and the PCE price index excluding food and energy rose 2.5%, both unchanged from the prior estimate. Profits from current production increased $206.0 billion in the third quarter, compared with an increase of $384.0 billion in the second quarter.

es.title: El PIB real de EE. UU. se revisa a 4,3 % anualizado en el 3T de 2026 desde 3,4 %, según la BEA
es.summary: La segunda estimación de la BEA muestra que el PIB real de EE. UU. creció a una tasa anual de 4,3 % en el tercer trimestre de 2026, frente a 2,2 % en el segundo trimestre. La cifra se revisó al alza en 0,9 puntos porcentuales frente a la estimación preliminar de 3,4 %, reflejando principalmente revisiones al alza de la inversión y del gasto de los consumidores. Las ventas finales reales a compradores privados domésticos aumentaron 5,8 %, mientras que el índice de precios del gasto de consumo personal (PCE) subió 2,1 % y el PCE sin alimentos ni energía subió 2,5 %, ambos sin cambios frente a la estimación previa. Las utilidades de la producción corriente aumentaron US$206,0 mil millones en el tercer trimestre, frente a un aumento de US$384,0 mil millones en el segundo.

briefs.title: Alianza analyst: USD/COP may reach 3,700-3,800 soon, then ease toward 3,000-3,200
briefs.summary: Felipe Campos of Alianza Valores y Fiduciaria said at a Valora Analitik forum that the dollar in Colombia, which closed above COP 3,600 the previous day, could rise to COP 3,700-3,800 in the coming days and weeks. He attributes the move to a global shock, a doubling of oil prices that he says lifted US inflation to 4% and led the Federal Reserve to resume rate hikes. In his view the medium-term trend favors the peso, with the dollar returning to COP 3,000-3,200. He says the tax reform's passage in Congress is the key catalyst: if at least 70% is approved, the dollar would peak at COP 3,700-3,800 and then fall, while a failed bill could send it to COP 4,300, 4,500 or even 5,500.

es.title: Analista de Alianza: dólar podría llegar a $3.700-$3.800 y luego bajar hacia $3.000-$3.200
es.summary: Felipe Campos, de Alianza Valores y Fiduciaria, afirmó en un foro de Valora Analitik que el dólar en Colombia, que cerró ayer por encima de $3.600, podría subir a $3.700-$3.800 en los próximos días y semanas. Atribuye el movimiento a un choque global: la duplicación de los precios del petróleo, que según él llevó la inflación de Estados Unidos al 4 % y llevó a la Reserva Federal a retomar el alza de tasas. En su visión, la tendencia de mediano plazo favorece al peso, con el dólar regresando a $3.000-$3.200. Señala que el trámite de la reforma tributaria en el Congreso es el catalizador clave: si se aprueba al menos el 70 %, el dólar tocaría un techo de $3.700-$3.800 y luego caería, mientras que un fracaso del proyecto podría llevarlo a $4.300, $4.500 o incluso $5.500.

briefs.title: Fed, CFPB set 2027 Regulation Z and M threshold at $76,300 for consumer credit, leases
briefs.summary: The Federal Reserve Board and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau announced the dollar thresholds that determine whether certain consumer credit and lease transactions in 2027 are covered by Regulation Z (Truth in Lending) and Regulation M (Consumer Leasing). Based on a 3.9 percent annual increase in the CPI-W as of June 1, 2026, the regulations generally will apply to consumer credit transactions and consumer leases of $76,300 or less in 2027. Private education loans and loans secured by real property, such as mortgages, are subject to Regulation Z regardless of the loan amount.

actors.reason: Transactions at or below the threshold receive the regulations' protections, but the source does not give the prior threshold to show how much coverage changes.

actors.reason: These loans are subject to Regulation Z regardless of amount, so the threshold does not determine whether they are covered.

es.title: Fed y CFPB fijan en US$76.300 el umbral 2027 de las Regulaciones Z y M para crédito al consumo
es.summary: La Junta de la Reserva Federal y la Oficina para la Protección Financiera del Consumidor (CFPB) anunciaron los umbrales en dólares que determinan si ciertas operaciones de crédito y arrendamiento al consumidor en 2027 están cubiertas por la Regulación Z (Veracidad en los Préstamos) y la Regulación M (Arrendamiento al Consumidor). Con base en un aumento anual de 3,9 % del CPI-W al 1 de junio de 2026, las regulaciones se aplicarán en general a operaciones de crédito al consumo y arrendamientos al consumidor de US$76.300 o menos en 2027. Los préstamos educativos privados y los préstamos garantizados con bienes raíces, como las hipotecas, están sujetos a la Regulación Z sin importar el monto.

briefs.title: Colombia's public debt reaches COP 1,200 trillion, 62.2% of GDP in October: MinHacienda data
briefs.summary: At end-October 2026, Colombia's public debt stood at COP 1,200 trillion, equal to 62.2% of projected 2026 GDP, according to Finance Ministry (MinHacienda) data reported by Valora Analitik. The ratio rose from 61.4% in September, an increase of 80 basis points. The stock grew about COP 14.7 trillion from September (COP 1,185 trillion) and about COP 19.6 trillion from October 2025 (COP 1,180 trillion). Domestic debt was COP 938.8 trillion (78.2% of the total) and external debt COP 261.5 trillion (21.8%). EAFIT analyst Diego Montañez noted three consecutive monthly increases and almost COP 40 trillion more debt since July.

es.title: Deuda pública de Colombia llegó a $1.200 billones, 62,2 % del PIB en octubre, según MinHacienda
es.summary: A octubre de 2026, el saldo de la deuda pública de Colombia se ubicó en $1.200 billones, equivalente al 62,2 % del PIB proyectado para 2026, según datos del Ministerio de Hacienda reportados por Valora Analitik. El indicador subió desde 61,4 % en septiembre, un aumento de 80 puntos básicos. El saldo creció unos $14,7 billones frente a septiembre ($1.185 billones) y unos $19,6 billones frente a octubre de 2025 ($1.180 billones). La deuda interna fue de $938,8 billones (78,2 % del total) y la externa de $261,5 billones (21,8 %). El analista de EAFIT Diego Montañez destacó tres meses consecutivos de aumentos y casi $40 billones más de deuda desde julio.

briefs.title: US agencies raise 2027 appraisal exemption threshold for higher-priced mortgages to $35,500

source.name: Federal Reserve Board (joint release with CFPB and OCC)

briefs.summary: The CFPB, the Federal Reserve Board and the OCC announced that the 2027 threshold for higher-priced mortgage loans subject to special appraisal requirements will rise from $34,200 to $35,500. It takes effect January 1, 2027. The adjustment is based on a 3.9 percent annual increase in the CPI-W as of June 1, 2026. Loans at or below the threshold are exempt from the requirements, which include a written appraisal based on a physical visit to the interior of the home.

Entrará en vigor el 1 de enero de 2027. El ajuste se basa en un aumento anual de 3,9 % del CPI-W al 1 de junio de 2026. briefs.title: Asian stocks fall on AI worries; US PCE data awaited, Brent near US$91 on Hormuz attacks
briefs.summary: Most Asian equity markets fell on Wednesday amid concerns over the sustainability of the AI trade, with Taiwan's index down 4.94%, the Kospi down 6.16% and the Nikkei 225 down 3.3%. European indices traded higher while investors awaited US October PCE data, which economists expect at 3.8% year on year versus 3.6% previously. Markets priced a 96.4% probability of a 25 basis point Fed hike at the December 8-9 meeting. Brent fell 0.5% to US$90.92 and WTI fell 0.9% to US$81.38 as signs of greater crude supply outweighed renewed attacks on shipping near the Strait of Hormuz.

audit.title: US real GDP revised up to 4.3% annual rate in Q3 2026 from 3.4%, BEA second estimate

issues: Actor 'US health care services' is rated 'adverse', but the source only says health care was the largest contributor to a downward revision of the services spending estimate, based on new Census survey data. The source does not say health care spending fell or that the sector was harmed, so the adverse impact is not supported. The same problem appears in the ES actor 'Servicios de salud de EE. UU.'.

Actor 'US investment in intellectual property products (software)' is rated 'favorable' on the basis of a statistical revision. The source attributes that revision to revised BLS Producer Price Index data for software publishing, which is a deflator/measurement change. It does not show improved conditions for the actor, so the 'favorable' impact claim overreaches the source.

Unknown 'How corporate profits were distributed across industries, which the release does not detail' is partly misleading. The release links Table 6.16D 'Corporate Profits by Industry', and the next release (Dec 23) explicitly includes industry and corporate profits data. The ES unknown has the same issue.

audit.title: Alianza analyst: USD/COP may reach 3,700-3,800 soon, then ease toward 3,000-3,200
Fed, CFPB set 2027 Regulation Z and M threshold at $76,300 for consumer credit, leases

issues: Actor 'Consumer lenders and lessors' is labeled impact 'mixed', but the source gives no basis for any positive or negative effect on lenders. The reason only restates that compliance scope depends on transaction size. The impact should be 'undetermined'.
Minor ES/EN mismatch: the Spanish title says only 'para crédito al consumo' and omits leases ('arrendamientos'), while the English title covers 'consumer credit, leases'.
Minor ES/EN mismatch: the Spanish lender actor reason drops 'disclosure and related' from 'disclosure and related requirements'.

audit.title: Colombia's public debt reaches COP 1,200 trillion, 62.2% of GDP in October: MinHacienda data

issues: eventDate is 2026-11-24, but the source article's publication date is 2026-11-25. The source never states when MinHacienda released the October figures. The only 24 November date is the timestamp on Montañez's embedded tweet, so 2026-11-24 is an inference rather than a stated event or publication date. Use 2026-11-25 unless a MinHacienda release date can be documented.

Actor 'Colombian national government (MinHacienda)' is labelled impact 'adverse', but the source never calls the rise adverse or names any consequence for the government. The source only says the ratio measures debt relative to the economy and that it rose from 61.4% to 62.2%. The reason given restates that fact and does not support an adverse impact. Change the impact to 'undetermined' or cite source support.

audit.title: US agencies raise 2027 appraisal exemption threshold for higher-priced mortgages to $35,500
Asian stocks fall on AI worries; US PCE data awaited, Brent near US$91 on Hormuz attacks

issues: The title says 'Brent near US$91 on Hormuz attacks' (ES: 'el Brent ronda US$91 por Ormuz'), which presents the attacks as the cause of the oil price level. The source says oil prices fell because signs of more crude supply outweighed the renewed Hormuz attacks. This causal attribution is unsupported and contradicts the draft's own summary. Suggested fix: 'Brent dips to near US$91 despite Hormuz attacks' / 'el Brent baja a cerca de US$91 pese a ataques en Ormuz'.

unsupported.text: If international LNG prices ease enough to meet Ecopetrol's competitiveness, profitability and risk criteria, purchases tend to resume and the terminals could receive cargoes near schedule. (ES: Si los precios internacionales del GNL bajan lo suficiente... las compras tienden a reanudarse y las terminales podrían recibir cargamentos cerca del cronograma.)
unsupported.why: Predicts Ecopetrol's own decisions and the cargo timing. This is a company-specific forecast, not a general economic mechanism. The source gives no resumption conditions or timeline, and the brief lists the timing as unknown.

unsupported.text: If Middle East tensions... keep prices high, the terminals tend to be ready but idle, and reliance on the SPEC plant tends to continue. (ES: ...las terminales tienden a quedar listas pero sin uso, y la dependencia de la planta de SPEC tiende a continuar.)
unsupported.why: Predicts specific outcomes for these terminals ('ready but idle'). It is not a widely accepted general mechanism, and neither the source nor the brief backs it.

unsupported.text: Anyone counting on new LNG import capacity feels it first, including users of the SPEC plant in Cartagena. (ES: Quien cuente con nueva capacidad de importación de GNL lo siente primero, incluidos los usuarios de la planta de SPEC en Cartagena.)
unsupported.why: Neither the source nor the brief says who is affected first or that SPEC users bear the impact. The brief marks SPEC's impact as undetermined.

unsupported.text: AES and the wind projects feel it later, around the first quarter of 2027. (ES: AES y los proyectos eólicos lo sienten después, hacia el primer trimestre de 2027.)
unsupported.why: Nothing links the LNG pause to AES or the wind projects. Q1 2027 is only the target for the JK1/JK2 FID, not a date when any impact is felt, and AES's impact is listed as undetermined.
